sections.h2: Where is Fort Collins, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Fort Collins is a home rule city and the seat of Larimer County, about 60 miles north of Denver and 45 miles south of Cheyenne, Wyoming. It sits at the base of the northern Front Range foothills along the Cache la Poudre River, with Spring Creek also running through town.

The city covers 58.5 square miles, stands near 5,000 feet in elevation and had 169,810 residents in the 2020 Census, making it the fourth most populous city in Colorado. Horsetooth Reservoir and Horsetooth Mountain mark the western skyline. The historic Old Town district sits next to the site of the original 1864 army post, and the city grew south from there through the late twentieth century.

Fort Collins uses a council-manager form of government. A mayor presides over a seven-member council, and six members are elected from districts.

sections.h2: Which office bills property tax for a Fort Collins home?
sections.html:
The city does not bill property tax. The Larimer County Treasurer mails the statements, collects the money and sends it to every taxing authority, including the school district, the city and special districts. The Treasurer's page is clear that the office does not decide how much tax is owed.

  • For the value of the property or how the tax was calculated, contact the Larimer County Assessor.
  • For payments, statements, delinquent balances and the lien sale, contact the Treasurer and Public Trustee, currently Irene Josey.
  • For help after a mortgage payoff, the Treasurer's site has a page on getting your tax statement once the lender no longer pays it.

The Public Trustee side of the office handles foreclosures and releases of deeds of trust, which follow Title 38 of the Colorado Revised Statutes.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 Larimer County tax due dates?
sections.html:
The Treasurer lists the first half due February 28, 2026, the second half due June 15, 2026, or a single full payment due April 30, 2026. Dates that land on a non-business day move to the next business day.

ItemLarimer County Treasurer
First halfFebruary 28, 2026
Full payment optionApril 30, 2026
Second halfJune 15, 2026
Payment styleTwo equal installments or one full payment; partial payments are not accepted
When tax becomes dueJanuary 1, for the previous year
2026 tax lien saleThursday, November 19, 2026, 8:00 a.m.

Because Larimer County says taxes become due on January 1 for the previous year, a seller closing mid-year should ask the closing company how the current year's share is handled.

sections.h2: Where is the Larimer County tax lien sale held?
sections.html:
The 2026 annual tax lien sale is scheduled for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch, 5280 Arena Circle, Loveland, in the Thomas McKee 4-H Community Building.

Fort Collins owners who still carry delinquent real estate tax should check with the Treasurer before that date. The Treasurer's site also lists information for tax lien investors, which is the other side of the same sale.

The site also posts a notice about courtesy orange tag notices for manufactured homes, which the office said it would post through September.

sections.h2: What payment tools does the Larimer County Treasurer offer?
sections.html:
The Treasurer offers online payment, receipts, eNotices and email reminders, and it has registered with EquaPay by Autoagent, formerly EscrowTaxes, for automated monthly payments. EquaPay is open to any Larimer County property that does not have taxes escrowed through a mortgage.

  • Title companies have a separate CTD login for Certificates of Taxes Due.
  • Mortgage companies have a mass payment option.
  • Owners can change their mailing address, search property and tax records, and print a receipt on the site.
  • Manufactured homes, personal property for businesses, and special assessments each have their own pages.

The county's system went offline for maintenance on Sunday, November 15, 2026, from 8:00 a.m. until about 2:00 p.m., a reminder that payment and search pages are not always available.

sections.h2: What does the climate mean for a Fort Collins house?
sections.html:
Fort Collins has a cold semi-arid climate, with about 15.88 inches of precipitation and 51.4 inches of snow in a typical year. The average temperature in December, the coldest month, is 31.1 degrees Fahrenheit, and snow can fall from early September through the end of May.

July is the warmest month, with a mean daily high of 87.4 degrees, and the record low is minus 41.

Flooding has a documented history. In late July 1997, a 31-hour storm dropped 10 to 14 inches of rain, the heaviest on record for an urban area of Colorado. Five people died, the city took about $5 million in damage, and Colorado State University's library flooded. A house near the Poudre River or Spring Creek may carry flood-related questions from buyers or lenders.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers around Fort Collins?
sections.html:
Colorado State University is the largest employer in Fort Collins, ahead of the University of Colorado Hospital Authority and the Poudre School District. The city's 2024 annual financial report lists the following.

Other industries include clean energy, bioscience and agri-tech, and the city has more than 20 breweries, including New Belgium and Odell. Federal agencies based in Fort Collins, including some USDA offices, employed over 5,000 people across Colorado as of 2025.

sections.h2: What schools, parks and libraries serve Fort Collins neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Public K to 12 schools in Fort Collins belong to the Poudre School District, which runs four comprehensive high schools: Fort Collins, Rocky Mountain, Poudre and Fossil Ridge. It also lists ten middle schools and 32 elementary schools.

The city has 875 acres of developed parks, including six community parks: City Park, Edora, Fossil Creek, Lee Martinez, Rolland Moore and Spring Canyon. The Poudre River Public Library District runs branches in Old Town, Harmony and Council Tree.

The school district is one of the taxing authorities on a Fort Collins bill, so which school boundary a house sits in is part of its tax area.

sections.h2: What is Larimer County, which taxes Fort Collins homes?
sections.html:
Larimer County covers 2,634 square miles along the Wyoming border, with 359,066 residents in 2020 and a 2025 estimate of 377,292. It was created November 1, 1861 and borders Weld, Boulder, Grand and Jackson counties in Colorado and Albany and Laramie counties in Wyoming.

Fort Collins and Loveland are the two cities, and the towns include Berthoud, Estes Park, Johnstown, Timnath, Wellington and Windsor. The census counted 158,769 housing units in the county, with 63.8% of occupied units owner-occupied and 36.2% rented. Interstate 25 and U.S. 34, 36, 87 and 287 cross the county.

Public schools in Fort Collins belong to the Poudre School District, which also serves Wellington, Timnath, Windsor, Laporte and Livermore.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Fort Collins?
faqs.a: You pay the Larimer County Treasurer, not the city. The Treasurer collects for the school district, the city, the county and special districts.

faqs.q: When is the Larimer County tax lien sale in 2026?
faqs.a: It is scheduled for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch in Loveland.

faqs.q: Can I pay Fort Collins property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer accepts two equal installments or one full payment, and does not accept partial payments. Owners without escrow can also enroll in EquaPay for monthly payments.

faqs.q: Which office do I call if I disagree with my value?
faqs.a: Call the Larimer County Assessor. The Treasurer states it does not determine the amount of tax and sends value questions to the Assessor.

faqs.q: How do I get a Certificate of Taxes Due in Larimer County?
faqs.a: Title companies use the Treasurer's CTD login, so ask your closing company to order it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fort Collins house that has tax due?
faqs.a: Yes. Any tax owed would be addressed at closing through the title company. If the account is delinquent, check with the Treasurer before the November lien sale.
